inputs.description: CloudWatch namespace. AWS/EC2 for CPUUtilization, NetworkOut, NetworkIn, DiskReadBytes, DiskWriteBytes, StatusCheckFailed. CWAgent for MemoryUtilization, DiskUtilization and anything else the CloudWatch agent publishes.
Metric that alarmed, e.g. CPUUtilization, MemoryUtilization, DiskUtilization, NetworkOut, StatusCheckFailed.

Value above which the metric counts as spiking. Pass the firing alarm's own threshold - the event carries it. The default of 70 only suits percentage metrics; for byte-valued metrics like NetworkOut it is meaningless, so always pass the real one.
ISO8601 UTC start of the window around the alarm, e.g. 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z.
ISO8601 UTC end of the window, e.g. 2026-09-03T12:30:00Z.

What to inspect on the host if a live look is needed. One of: triage (default - load, top CPU/memory processes, disk, boot time), top_cpu, top_memory, disk_usage, memory_usage, network_connections, running_services, failed_services, recent_logins, shell_history, cron_jobs, recent_syslog, process_tree, boot_time, package_changes.
auto = only look inside the host when SSM history does not explain the spike (default, cheapest). always = always inspect. never = metrics and SSM history only.

params.command: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace {{ Inputs.namespace }} --metric-name {{ Inputs.metric_name }} --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value={{ Inputs.instance_id }} --start-time {{ Inputs.window_start }} --end-time {{ Inputs.window_end }} --period 60 --statistics Average Maximum --region {{ Inputs.region }} --output json
aws ssm list-commands --instance-id {{ Inputs.instance_id }} --max-results 50 --region {{ Inputs.region }} --output json

llm_description:
Investigates any EC2 instance alarm end to end and says what caused it - CPU, memory, disk, network or status check.

First it correlates the alarming CloudWatch metric with AWS SSM Run Command history, looking back 30 minutes before the spike, because the command that causes a spike always precedes it. If that identifies a likely cause it reports the exact command, when it ran and its comment, and stops there.

If SSM history does not explain it, it inspects the host over SSM and returns live state: load, top CPU and memory consumers, disk, memory, network connections, services, logins, shell history, cron jobs and timers, system logs, or package changes - set host_action to choose, default 'triage'.

Set namespace and metric_name to whatever alarmed (AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization, NetworkOut, StatusCheckFailed; CWAgent MemoryUtilization, DiskUtilization). Pass spike_threshold from the alarm itself - the default 70 suits percentages only and is wrong for byte-valued metrics.

Read-only. It never kills, restarts or reconfigures anything.
